teaching.en: A measurable goal says how much you want to improve.

teaching.explanationEs: Incluye un número o criterio que permita comprobar el resultado.

teaching.en: Frequency tells us how often: twice a week or every day.

answer.text: I recognise familiar words, but I find spelling new words difficult. My goal is to spell sixteen of twenty words correctly in two weeks. Every evening, I will spend ten minutes testing five words without looking at my notes. Then I will correct my errors to learn the difficult spellings. I will keep dated word lists and scores so that I can see my progress. At the end of two weeks, I will compare my first and final lists and check how many words I can spell correctly.

prompt.es: Escribe el plan de Luis en 80–100 palabras con frecuencia y evidencia.

answer.text: I can explain my ideas, but I often forget past verb forms. In two weeks, I want to use nine of ten past forms correctly. I will write a short diary entry on Tuesday, Thursday and Sunday. Each session will take fifteen minutes. I will check the verbs to find and correct my mistakes. I will save the original and corrected entries as evidence. After two weeks, I will compare mistakes in my first and last entries so that I can measure my progress.
